clue.text: Monet rated badly in new gallery

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: the painter's name and the verb taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A critic panned Monet's pictures at a recently opened exhibition space.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is the London gallery of modern art that opened in 2000 on the Thames at Bankside.
explanation.definitionFit: Opened in 2000, the London museum of modern and contemporary art is a relatively recent addition to the capital's galleries.

clue.text: Course of action queen, perhaps, set up with king

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a queen is a female cat; perhaps marks it as one example
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone describes a royal plan of action involving a queen and a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks royal next to 'king', but here it is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is an approach or line of policy, from the sailing sense of a change in heading.

clue.text: Ready for release after time in part of ship

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ready is slang for cash, and cash paid to free a captive is a ransom

explanation.surface: A prisoner held in a ship's quarters is nearly ready to be let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After time' places the money word after the T. 'Ready' looks like an adjective but is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is the flat stern section or a crossbeam at the back of a vessel's hull.

clue.text: Diversified combination of minerals and oil is making someone very rich

indicators.note: diversified means varied or spread about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor with a spread of mining and petroleum interests is getting wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A millionairess is a woman whose wealth runs to at least a million, so she is very rich.

clue.text: Energetic type upset lots of people in party

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other, here inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the word goes upwards

parts.note: many means lots, used as a noun for a great number of people

explanation.surface: A lively guest annoyed a crowd at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a figurative name for a tirelessly energetic person, from the electrical generator.

clue.text: Prevailed over son that's abandoned post

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the longer word wraps around the single letter

parts.note: to reign is to prevail or hold sway
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A ruler's son walked out of his role after holding power over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'defeated' but means the letter is covered by the bigger word.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a job or office, so resigned means abandoned one's post.

clue.text: Leaders of social workers are threatening strike

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: The heads of a social care union say staff may walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' sits at the end looking like industrial action, but it means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To swat is to hit sharply, as at a fly, so it is a synonym of strike.

clue.text: Survive as partners, heart-broken?

parts.note: a couple speaking as partners would say we

indicators.note: something broken is shattered and reassembled anyhow, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple wonders whether they can get through heartbreak together.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'heart-broken' disguises a word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm or crisis is to come through it intact, so it means survive.

clue.text: Proposing explanations in article on old rebellion

parts.note: the definite article
O is the abbreviation for old
a rising is an uprising or revolt

explanation.surface: A historian puts forward theories in a piece of writing about a past revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the rebellion word after the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorising is forming theories, which are proposed accounts of why something happens.

clue.text: Place in series for old movie star

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here inside the series word

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things
PL is the map abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: A spot in a film series is found for a veteran screen actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Chaplin was the great silent-film comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was a famous star of silent cinema, so an old movie star in the film-history sense.

clue.text: Wise crossing immense country in banger?

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so the outer word stretches over the other piece

parts.note: sage as an adjective means wise
the United States, a vast country

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders about driving across a huge land in an old jalopy.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage, though it also means a battered old car, which is the sense the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a banger is a sausage; the question mark flags the less obvious sense of the word.

clue.text: United captain changed? That's surprising

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A football fan reacts to news that the club has a new skipper.
explanation.walkthrough: United suggests a football club such as Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unanticipated was not expected, which is what makes it surprising.

clue.text: Scientist whose work is on shaky ground?

definitions.text: Scientist whose work is on shaky ground?

parts.words: Scientist whose work is on shaky ground?
parts.note: surface reading: a researcher whose theories are poorly founded
setter's reading: literally trembling earth, the subject of an earthquake specialist

explanation.walkthrough: 'On shaky ground' is the idiom for unsound reasoning, but read literally it means earth that is quaking.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist records and studies earthquake tremors, literal shaking of the ground, with instruments.

clue.text: Sporting pursuit excited ace, perhaps

indicators.note: excited means agitated and stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: both words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tennis player chasing a game gets worked up about a possible ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is a cross-country game in which runners follow a trail of scattered paper, a sporting chase.

clue.text: Preparing for combat with male in a place for fighting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other, here within the fighting place

parts.note: a boxing ring is where bouts are fought
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A boxer gets ready for a bout by stepping into the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Arming means equipping with weapons, which is getting ready to fight.

clue.text: Non-Asian movies that may have roles for Indians

definitions.text: Non-Asian movies that may have roles for Indians

parts.words: Non-Asian movies that may have roles for Indians
parts.note: surface reading: films made outside Asia that still cast actors from India
setter's reading: Native Americans, the stock adversaries in cowboy films

explanation.walkthrough: 'Indians' suggests India, which 'Non-Asian' seems to rule out, but the old film genre uses the word for Native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboy films set in the American frontier traditionally include Native American characters, hence the old phrase about roles for Indians.

clue.text: Main picture airline's first showing in second flight

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: showing in means appearing inside, so the letter goes within the flight word

parts.note: flight in the sense of fleeing is an escape

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An airline's headline image appears in the second departure of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea. The chosen letter goes inside the flight word, and S comes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting or view of the ocean, and the main is a literary term for the sea.

clue.text: Inspected cotton fabric cut the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: denim is a sturdy cotton twill
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: An inspector checked jeans material that had been badly tailored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut the wrong way' reads like poor tailoring, but 'cut' is a verb supplying letters, and the whole pair is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Examined means looked at carefully, which is what inspecting something involves.

clue.text: Period in which monarch managed to produce desired order

indicators.note: in which tells us the following pieces sit inside the period word

parts.note: an age is a period of time
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A historian describes an era when a ruler kept things running smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to set them out in the order one wants.

clue.text: Fighting that follows direction to start shooting

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the film director's call to begin filming

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' seems to belong with 'Fighting' but means filming; the second definition is a film director's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means military combat and is also what a film director calls out when the cameras are to roll.

clue.text: Frantically liaise about resistance from part of Middle East

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the single letter
frantically means in a wild hurry, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Diplomats rush to talk to an opposition movement in the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Israeli is the adjective for things or people belonging to Israel, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Star group disrupted by a violent female

indicators.note: disrupted by means broken into, so the following letter is pushed inside

parts.note: Virgo is a constellation, a group of stars
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity band has its gig wrecked by an aggressive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star group' suggests a pop act but is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, aggressive or bad-tempered woman.

clue.text: Somebody complaining about favourite undergarment and footwear

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the complainer word wraps around what follows

parts.note: a carper is someone who carps, or finds fault
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
a slip is a woman's underskirt

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about their best-loved underwear and shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: A carper is a fault-finder, from carp, to grumble; it is split so that its middle holds the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet slipper is a soft indoor shoe, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Copied contents of paper with note appended

indicators.note: appended means tacked on at the end, so the note follows the first piece
the contents are what lies inside, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: the inner letters of the word
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone copied what was in a document and added a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appended' says the note goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or imitate them, so aped means copied.

clue.text: One can't remember if one has it

definitions.text: One can't remember if one has it

parts.words: One can't remember if one has it
parts.note: surface reading: someone unsure whether they own a certain thing
setter's reading: the condition itself is the inability to recall

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as forgetting whether you possess something; in fact having the condition is what stops you remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: This condition is a loss of memory, so a sufferer cannot recall things.

clue.text: An irritatingly silly bloke in European city

parts.note: taken as written
a twerp is an annoying, foolish person

explanation.surface: A tiresome fool turns up in a city on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port city in Belgium, in Europe.

clue.text: Weapon people get, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth and so on

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.surface: People acquire arms regardless of the risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The odds' looks like betting or chances, but means the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a fencing sword, so a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Support brass, for example, as requirement for renewed effort

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
brass instruments are wind instruments

explanation.surface: Backing the brass section of a band is needed for a fresh push.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is a burst of new energy after tiredness, which lets someone carry on with fresh vigour.
